html:
The Pocumtuck were an Algonquian people of the middle Connecticut River valley, centred near today's Deerfield, Massachusetts. They farmed maize on the rich river meadows and fished the spring runs of shad and salmon at the falls.

They traded wampum and furs with the Dutch and English. In the 1660s they were drawn into a war with the Mohawk of the Haudenosaunee, who destroyed their main fort around 1664. English settlers then founded Deerfield on their fields. Survivors fought the English in King Philip's War of 1675 to 1676 and then fled north or west, joining the Abenaki and the Mahican. Their neighbours included the Nipmuc.
